name: Zachary Fenstermacher
languages: Pennsylvania Dutch (his grandparents' language, which he grew up in)
equipment: Heavy coat: an Army surplus field jacket with a Penn State patch
Silver knife: his grandmother's silver fruit knife, which she said to take 'to the lake, because you never know'
A few good books: a German folklore dictionary, a Pennsylvania German almanac of 1888, his thesis draft in a binder
Library card: Pattee Library, The Pennsylvania State University
A letter of enrollment, and a letter from Opal Seeley granting him access to the ice company papers
Tape recorder: a cassette recorder with four tapes of interviews with old Pocono ice cutters
Chalk, a candle, a box of iron nails and a hank of red thread, because folklorists carry them and so did his grandmother
A coat that is not warm enough (the field jacket)
features: Seen It in a Book (Educated origin: once per long rest he recalls one useful fact about history, science, law, geography or a book without a check; advantage on Research checks in a library, archive or registry; he reads old handwriting and legal language without a check)

Old Lore (Occultist: once the party has seen a creature or clear sign of it, he spends an action and makes an INT (Occult) check, DC 10 + its CR; on a success the GM tells him one of its rules the party has not yet learned; once per creature per long rest. Advantage on Occult checks for rites and wards, done in half the time)
The Right Things in the Bag (Occultist: once per scenario, when a rite or ward needs a common object he could plausibly have packed, a candle, a nail, red thread, chalk, a bell, he has it)
Steeped in It (Occultist, 2nd level: advantage on fear checks against the sign of a horror, DC 10, and whenever the party learns one of a creature's rules he loses 1 Dread)
Tradition: Folklorist (Occultist, 3rd level: advantage on Persuasion checks with the old, and an interview with the oldest person in a place always yields one true clue toward a creature's rule)

Library Privileges (Student background: he can get into any academic library and many private ones, a professor will usually see him, and people explain things to him in more detail than they would to anyone else)
traits: The Right Things in the Bag (1/scenario)

personality.traits: I get excited about the wrong things at the wrong time. I write down what people say word for word. I trust old men on porches more than books.
personality.ideals: Folklore is what ordinary people knew that nobody wrote down. Somebody has to write it down before they're gone.
personality.bonds: My grandmother in Kutztown, who taught me which stories are true. My thesis advisor, who thinks ice cutters are a dull subject. Leopold Kistler, eighty-nine, the last Lantern Lake cutter, on his porch in Tobyhanna.
personality.flaws: I want it to be real. I have wanted it to be real for as long as I can remember. That makes me careless.

appearance: Twenty-six, lanky and pale with a big Adam's apple, wire-rimmed glasses, long brown hair in a ponytail, a field jacket over a Fair Isle sweater, a tape recorder over one shoulder.
backstory: Zachary Fenstermacher is a doctoral student in folklore at Penn State, from a Pennsylvania Dutch family in Berks County that still keeps a hex sign on the barn because it is pretty. His thesis is on the work songs, customs and beliefs of the Pocono natural-ice industry, which died in the 1930s, and for two years he has been driving round the mountains with a tape recorder interviewing the last old men who cut ice. One of them, Leopold Kistler, eighty-nine, who worked the Lantern Lake channels in 1911 to 1915, told him on his porch in Tobyhanna in July that the Lantern Lake gangs worked hooded at night 'on account of Old Glass', and would say no more, and cried. Zachary wrote to the camp and Opal Seeley invited him for the closing weekend to see the ice company's papers in the Office attic. He came on the bus to Larkin Corners and Roscoe gave him a lift. (Hook: the past. He is the door to the night log, and the one who has already heard the name Old Glass.)
